methods.name: Project links
methods.unit: outputs linked to a FORRT project
methods.checks: The supplied output lists and their project associations.
methods.canShow: Which outputs are connected to a named FORRT project.
methods.cannotShow: Whether an unlinked output belongs to a project without checking its source.

methods.name: DOI validity
methods.unit: recorded DOIs verified with their registration agency
methods.checks: Crossref records and DataCite records when Crossref has no record.
methods.canShow: Whether a recorded DOI is registered and where.
methods.cannotShow: Whether that output was cited, mentioned, or used.

methods.name: DOI citation searches
methods.unit: DOI outputs with complete OpenAlex and OpenCitations retrieval
methods.checks: Citing records in OpenAlex and OpenCitations for each recorded DOI.
methods.canShow: Which documents these services link as citations to an output.
methods.cannotShow: A complete census of citations; the services overlap and may disagree.

methods.name: Google Scholar lists
methods.unit: profile outputs whose full citing list was downloaded
methods.checks: Citing lists for outputs on the FORRT Google Scholar profile.
methods.canShow: Additional citing works, including some without DOIs.
methods.cannotShow: Citations for outputs outside that profile or entries behind blocked pages.

methods.name: Web searches
methods.unit: outputs with a completed planned web search
methods.checks: Planned public web queries for each output.
methods.canShow: Candidate pages and snippets worth inspecting.
methods.cannotShow: That all web mentions were found or that a snippet proves use.

methods.name: Altmetric pages
methods.unit: FORRT website DOI badges with a populated Altmetric page
methods.checks: Public Altmetric pages for DOIs badged on FORRT's publications page.
methods.canShow: Provider-reported attention and labelled mention or reader counts.
methods.cannotShow: Every individual mention, other DOI versions, or untracked attention.

methods.name: Retrieved source text
methods.unit: outputs with at least one retrieved source passage
methods.checks: Accessible pages and full text associated with candidate mentions.
methods.canShow: What a source actually says near a FORRT reference.
methods.cannotShow: That the reference describes adoption or an outcome without reading it.

methods.name: Human cross-check
methods.unit: sample records assessed by a human reviewer
methods.checks: A retained blind sample of suggested evidence classifications.
methods.canShow: How often the automated interpretation agrees with reviewers.
methods.cannotShow: A defensible total of uses or outcomes until the sample is assessed.

impact.selectionNote: Illustrative public-source examples, not an exhaustive or human-calibrated total of FORRT impact.

cases.title: FORRT terms shaped a UK research-practice survey
cases.claim: A UK Reproducibility Network survey used the FORRT glossary to define 14 open-research practice areas and linked respondents to it for explanation.
cases.source_kind: Research article describing its survey methods
cases.limit: This documents use of glossary terminology in a survey. It does not show that FORRT changed respondents' practices.

cases.title: A Johns Hopkins course assigned the FORRT glossary
cases.claim: The Fall 2023 Research Landscape syllabus at Johns Hopkins School of Education assigned students to read six FORRT glossary entries, summarise them, check another source, and post the definitions to a class discussion.
cases.source_name: Johns Hopkins School of Education course syllabus
cases.source_kind: Instructor-hosted syllabus PDF for a named university course
cases.limit: The syllabus documents an assignment, not whether students completed it or what they learned.

cases.title: A health-research survey presented FORRT definitions
cases.claim: An international survey of complementary, alternative, and integrative medicine researchers used the FORRT glossary to explain open-science practices to respondents.
cases.source_kind: Peer-reviewed research article describing its survey methods
cases.limit: The authors report using glossary definitions in the survey. The article does not show that FORRT changed respondents' behaviour or the study's findings.

cases.title: An online statistics textbook uses the FORRT glossary in an exercise
cases.claim: An online statistics textbook reproduces the FORRT glossary's QRP entry, then asks learners to apply it to a worked example.
cases.source_name: Data Analysis for the Language Sciences
cases.limit: The material is publicly available, but enrolment, exercise completion, and learning outcomes are not reported.

cases.title: An applied-research review credits FORRT for its definitions table
cases.claim: A review of preregistration in applied research labels its key-definitions table as drawn from the FORRT glossary, with exceptions stated in the table heading.
cases.source_name: University of Greenwich accepted manuscript of Evans et al.
cases.source_kind: Author-accepted manuscript of a peer-reviewed review article
cases.limit: This is documented terminology reuse in a review. It does not show a change in applied research practice.

cases.title: A field-specific glossary credits FORRT as inspiration
cases.claim: The fNIRS Glossary Project explicitly says it was inspired by FORRT's glossary project.
cases.limit: This establishes acknowledged inspiration, not which design features were copied or how researchers used the new glossary.

cases.title: Surrey points researchers to the FORRT glossary
cases.claim: The University of Surrey's open-research guidance links to the FORRT glossary as a way to learn the terminology.
cases.limit: A recommendation is visible; readership, classroom use, and learning outcomes are not reported.

cases.title: UNESCO lists a FORRT teaching syllabus
cases.claim: UNESCO's open-science resource hub describes FORRT's nine-week syllabus and links to it as a teaching resource.
cases.limit: The entry describes availability and potential adaptation. It does not identify a course that used the syllabus.

cases.title: COS transferred educational resources into FORRT
cases.claim: The Center for Open Science reports that it moved Open Scholarship Knowledge Base resources to FORRT and combined the two collections.
cases.limit: The partner reports a resource and infrastructure contribution. The announcement does not measure subsequent use or learning.

cases.title: FORRT helps maintain a replication journal
cases.claim: Replication Research names FORRT and the Münster Center for Open Science as organisations maintaining the journal.
cases.limit: This documents an ongoing organisational role, not journal reach or downstream research effects.

cases.title: FORRT submitted evidence to a UK Parliament inquiry
cases.claim: The Science and Technology Committee received FORRT's written evidence for its inquiry on reproducibility and research integrity.
cases.limit: A submission documents participation. It does not show that Parliament adopted a FORRT recommendation.
cases.output_title: Written Evidence Submitted by the FORRT (Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training) (RRE0080)

cases.title: An external analysis uses FReD replication data
cases.claim: A public PSY6422 analysis says its effect-level data came from the FORRT Replication Database and documents cleaning, study-level aggregation, and visualisation of those records.
cases.source_kind: Public student analysis and documented workflow
cases.limit: This documents reported use of FReD data in a student project. It is not a peer-reviewed evaluation or evidence of downstream policy or research change.
